items.title: fix: harden visual benchmark artifact workflow
items.body:
## Incident evidence
The first parallel production dispatch exposed a transient source response: run `31530474321` received SHA-256 `88c98e6e...` for the TPS5430 URL instead of the registered `3d75dd36...` and correctly failed before scoring. Four immediate operator downloads and retry run `31530642843` all received the registered bytes; the retry completed all 21 RapidOCR cases. This is CDN inconsistency, not a registry revision update.

The successful jobs also exposed a non-portable absolute path in the checksum file and a Node 20 deprecation warning from upload-artifact v4.

## Fix
- retry only freshly downloaded SHA-256 mismatches, at most 3 attempts with bounded linear backoff
- continue to fail corrupted cache and every non-hash contract error immediately
- emit basename-relative portable checksum records
- update both artifact publishers to the official pinned upload-artifact v7.0.1 commit
- add regression coverage for transient mismatch recovery and final fail-closed behavior

## Verification
- `python -m ruff format --check .`
- `python -m ruff check .`
- `python -m pytest -q` (157 passed, 1 skipped)
- first-run text artifact and retry RapidOCR artifact both independently rehashed successfully after download

After merge I will rerun the workflow and verify `sha256sum -c` directly from the downloaded artifact directory.

Fixes TokitoAI/tokito#353
Advances TokitoAI/tokito#350

items.title: Add a survivorship-free benchmark rule: beats_benchmark_symbol
items.body:
Every benchmark this harness had — `beats_buy_hold`, `beats_exposure_matched`, and `enablement_gate`'s internals — derives from **the snapshot's own universe**. §48 measured what that costs:

| | 2000-2006 |
|---|---|
| equal-weight buy-and-hold | +138.74% |
| **SPY over the identical bars** | **+8.68%** |
| | **+130pp of pure survivorship** |

Every EDGE claim from §14 onward was scored against the inflated number.

## What this adds

`beats_benchmark_symbol` races **one named instrument**. An index ETF's price already reflects constituent changes — names that failed left the index and took their losses with them — so the benchmark carries no survivorship.

- `backtest.benchmark_stats()` **reuses** `buy_and_hold_return` and `buy_and_hold_drawdown`, which already worked on a single symbol. Charged the same slippage and fees, entered at the same bar — like-for-like in everything except which instruments it holds.
- **Both `Result` construction sites** populate it. The ensemble path is the one every gate takes; the single-strategy path is the one unit tests take. A field on only one looks correct under test and scores `None` in production — there's a test per path.
- `gatespec` requires an explicit `symbol`, **inside the frozen hash**. Otherwise swapping SPY for a flattering instrument after registration would leave the goalpost unchanged.
- An unmeasurable benchmark **FAILS**, never silently passes — the §33 RUN 1 precedent, where checks that quietly didn't run produced a VALIDATED verdict.
- maxDD is **reported, never gated**. Matched drawdown was §44's question and was rejected there.

## The residual asymmetry — documented in the rule, not hidden

The **strategy still trades a survivor-only universe**, so the comparison runs in its favour. **A FAIL is decisive; a PASS is not.** This reduces the bias, it does not remove it.

## Verification

- **Regression:** re-ran `s48d` against the new code. Both arms reproduced §48 **exactly** — baseline −7.71% / PF 0.367 / maxDD 10.99% / 54 trades, `no_drawdown_rail` +61.67% / PF 1.424 / maxDD 16.65% / 3084 trades. The new fields do not perturb the simulator.
- 17 tests; **8 mutations**, all caught, all restores byte-identical by `md5 -q`: `>=`→`>`, missing benchmark passing, wrong-symbol guard removed, ensemble site losing the field, absent returning `0.0` instead of `None`, benchmark scored frictionlessly, `symbol` no longer required, drawdown detail dropped.
- 1419 → **1436** tests. `ruff` clean.
- No config touched, nothing enabled, `mode: paper`.

items.title: feat: score corrected transcripts and republish WER
items.body:
## Context

Every published number in this repository measures raw ASR output or
diarization. Nothing measures the correction lane — the lane that is the
product's actual review path: the operator supplies a terminology list and the
model repairs the transcript against it, with no human editing pass. There was
no way to answer "did correction help, and did it break anything".

Building that measurement surfaced a metric bug that had to be fixed first, and
fixing it moves two published numbers.

**The normalization bug.** `docs/contracts/scoring.md` declares punctuation
*removal*; `metrics.py` replaced punctuation with *spaces*. Reference `dont` vs
hypothesis `don't` therefore normalized to `dont` vs `don t` — one substitution
plus one insertion, WER 2.0 instead of 0. Correction routinely rewrites
punctuation, so scoring corrected text under the old normalizer would count
punctuation edits as word errors. The contract was right; the code was wrong.

**Republication (maintainer-approved 2026-08-11).** Fixing it changes WER only —
CER is mathematically invariant because character scoring strips all whitespace
after normalization:

| Published value | Before | After |
|---|---:|---:|
| Korean VibeVoice WER | 0.128 | 0.141 |
| Italian MOSS WER | 0.081 | 0.085 |
| All CER values | unchanged | unchanged |

Term recall, omissions, and backchannel 7/7 do not move.

## Changes

- **`metrics.py`** deletes punctuation instead of replacing it with spaces, per
  the declared contract. Apostrophe (ASCII and typographic), hyphen, NFKC,
  case, whitespace, and Italian-diacritic behavior are pinned by tests.
- **`score.py`** opens its output exclusive-create; an existing scores artifact
  is preserved instead of truncated (judgment rule 3: artifacts are
  create-only).
- **Republication in the same change**: `benchmarks/published-results.json`
  (with fresh artifact SHA-256 provenance), all ten READMEs, the four generated
  figures, both historical verdict docs, the app profile resource and the app
  test that pins those values, and a new `D36 [maintainer]` decision record in
  `PROJECT.md`.
- **`score_corrected.py`** (new): scores a correction run's raw and corrected
  output against one reference. Before trusting any number it verifies the
  correction respected the contract — segment count, speakers, timestamps,
  source, language, confidence all unchanged — and rejects with the offending
  segment and field named. Reports per-metric directional deltas,
  applied-vs-review counts, and correction-safety classification.
- **Correction-safety counting**: an applied change is evaluated only when
  exactly one reference segment has the identical time interval; raw and
  corrected CER/WER edit counts are then compared Pareto-style (`closer`,
  `further`, `mixed`, `unchanged`, plus `correct_to_incorrect` when a correct
  segment was rewritten wrong). If any applied change cannot be aligned,
  `correction_made_worse_count` is `null` rather than a misleading zero, with
  the observed count and unevaluated list alongside.
- **`compare_correction_paths.py`** (new): the four-state harness — no-glossary
  ASR, decode-time glossary ASR, each corrected — emitting one create-only
  verdict JSON with the three deltas that matter: decode-time injection gain,
  correction gain, correction gain without decode-time injection. Thresholds
  live in a versioned JSON file; every value is deliberately `null` and the
  verdict stays `passed: null` until the maintainer sets standards.

## Validation

- Scoring suite: **69/69** (baseline before the change: 49/49, zero failures).
- Contract checker: all three schemas pass.
- README checker: all ten files match the declaration.
- Figure suite: 6/6 after regenerating the four SVGs.
- `swift build` passes; the app test target passes **45 tests in 7 suites**
  after updating the two pinned WER values.
- Red-then-green evidence recorded for the normalizer fix (4 failures before),
  the corrected scorer, and the harness.
- A synthetic four-state demonstration produces the expected deltas, including
  one deliberate `correct_to_incorrect` regression caught by the safety count.

Not verified: a live correction turn against a real model — the harness
consumes completed run directories and this host has no pinned model caches.
The fixture demonstration covers the tooling, not model behavior.

## Notes for review

- `Tests/MaccheroniAppTests/AppShellTests.swift` is also touched by #9 in a
  different region; whichever merges second rebases trivially.
- A follow-up contract doc should specify the corrected-score JSON shape and
  the four-state verdict semantics; flagged in the report rather than edited,
  since `docs/contracts/` changes deserve their own review.
- The threshold placeholders in
  `benchmarks/scripts/scoring/correction-comparison-thresholds.json` are yours
  to set; the harness reports `not_configured` until then.

items.title: feat(benchmark): preregister player-disjoint representation benchmark (scoutlens-qop.1)
items.body:
Closes `scoutlens-qop.1`. Decision record: **D041**.

Freezes the confirmatory benchmark for `scoutlens-qop` **before any learned model is fitted**.

- **Protocol hash** `886ba315b587a91d0fa9ab5c7387f172f8957cf2cfde8a39a65216cb4ff31f1d`
- **Split assignment digest** `715bdb90af59860c2510d6a69f43970c9734bef4e4e061740658d2496c30d96a`

## Why a new design rather than reusing the published one

The published temporal-retrieval result fits the scaler on the same population it scores. That is correct for a **descriptive** feasibility claim and wrong for a **confirmatory** one. Three things change:

1. **The split unit is the human**, not `(player_id, competitionId)` — no model can be fitted on one half of a person and scored on the other.
2. **The scaler is fit on the training split only** — a deliberate departure from D008.
3. **Candidate pools are within-split** — a test query can never retrieve a training player.

## What landed

| | |
|---|---|
| `docs/representation-benchmark-protocol.md` | The preregistration, 14 sections |
| `src/scoutlens/benchmark/` | Executable copy — the hash is computed over `protocol.py` |
| `tests/benchmark/` | 30 tests |
| `artifacts/benchmark/` | Split manifest + frozen baseline reference values |

1,257 eligible players → **753 / 251 / 253**, role-stratified, deterministic via `sha256(f"{seed}:{player_id}")` rather than a shuffled RNG, so the assignment is order-independent and adding a player perturbs only its own position.

The canonical **28 / 30** shared feature sets existed only in prose since D021. They are now executable and fail at import if the derivation stops matching the frozen counts.

## Reviewer notes

**Do not compare split MRR to the published numbers.** Pools shrink from 1,257 to 753/251/253, so retrieval is mechanically easier and MRR is mechanically higher (Baseline B: 0.320 train, 0.429 validation, against 0.279 published). Nothing improved — the pool shrank. Only the **within-split paired delta** is the object of study. The protocol says this in three places because it is the easiest thing here to misread.

**The test-set lock is mechanical, not a promise.** `assert_test_set_unlocked()` reads `docs/decisions-log.md` for the protocol hash and raises otherwise; `evaluate_split(..., TEST)` additionally requires an explicit opt-in. Editing `PROTOCOL` changes the hash and re-locks the split. This was observed working in both directions during development: the runner skipped test before D041 and evaluated it after, and the precision fix below re-locked it until D041 was corrected.

**Leakage is proven behaviourally, not by inspection.** `test_leakage.py` corrupts every validation and test feature value by six orders of magnitude and asserts the fitted scaler and the whole training evaluation do not move.

## Two findings recorded rather than smoothed over

**1. The subgroup gate is inert at this split size.** The frozen rule gates only role subgroups with ≥100 queries, but the test split's largest is Defender at **95** (Midfielder 90, Forward 48, Goalkeeper 20). As specified it gates **zero** roles.

Counting split sizes by role is design information, not outcome information, so establishing this did not open the test set. The threshold is **not** retuned here — changing a preregistered decision threshold is a charter decision, not an executor's call. Routed to `scoutlens-qop.5` (P1, flagged for human decision) with three options and a recommendation, and wired as a blocker of `scoutlens-qop.4` so the KEEP/DROP call cannot be taken under a dead gate.

**2. A real reproducibility defect, found and fixed.** The first two runs produced different scaler bytes — 18 of 28 columns off by 1–2 ULPs (`39.66938688224109` vs `39.669386882241085`), from Polars' parallel sum reduction. Metrics were already bit-identical because ranks are integers, but an artifact that cannot be regenerated byte-for-byte is not publishable under D040 §4.1. Fixed by quantizing fitted statistics to 12 significant digits, at ~1e-12 relative per z-score.

## One contract boundary crossed, deliberately

Versioning the two artifacts needed a `.gitignore` negation, which **D040 lists as Denied to a modeling bead** — and `qop.1` is labelled `modeling`. The collision was raised and authorized before the edit rather than taken silently. It follows the documented `artifacts/README.md` pattern the six existing result summaries already use, and is recorded in D041.

## Verification

```
uv run --frozen pytest -q          -> 328 passed, 9 skipped in 8.62s  (was 298)
uv run --frozen pytest tests/benchmark -q -> 30 passed
uv run --frozen ruff check .       -> All checks passed!
uv run --frozen mypy src/scoutlens -> Success: no issues found in 58 source files
uv build                           -> scoutlens-0.2.0.dev0 sdist + wheel
```

Two consecutive `--with-test` runs compared as canonical JSON: **identical for both artifacts**, excluding the `_manifest.generated_at` stamp that the existing `run_manifest` pattern embeds by design.

Budgets: **19.2 s** wall clock against an 1,800 s limit; artifacts **15.2 + 11.5 KiB** against 5 MiB. `docs/decisions-log.md` is append-only: **+78 / −0**.

items.title: feat(benchmarks): a memory-benchmark harness outside the package (#1029)
items.body:
Builds the memory-benchmark harness for the pilot pre-registered in #1029.

**No scored evaluation run has been executed.** Not one question has been answered by a live model in this lane. Every run mode defaults to `SMOKE`; `SCORED` is refused unless the operator states #1029's ground rule 1 is discharged; the mode is written into every manifest, so "has a scored run happened?" is answerable from artifacts rather than from memory. Issue #1029 was not edited.

Refs: #1029, #1034
Fixes #1064
Fixes #1069

---

## Successor pre-flight (ADR-0138 §4, written before any edit)

I took this lane over under the ADR-0138 §1 handoff comment on this PR. Round 8 is mine
and the predecessor is not running it.

**Inherited:** `bench/memory-harness` @ `3fee41c0`, tree clean, gate green, PR draft.
**Touched to close the standing finding:** `benchmarks/memory/run.py`,
`benchmarks/README.md`, `tests/benchmarks/test_run_end_to_end.py` — inside the original
fence and inside the predecessor's own diff.
**Not touched:** `src/ai_assistant/**`, `docs/adr/**`, `docs/roadmap.md`, `CLAUDE.md`,
`CONTRIBUTING.md`, `.github/**`, `pyproject.toml` (its two entries stand unchanged).
**Governing:** ADR-0138 §§1–4 (the handoff and what a successor is), ADR-0136 (gate
anchors), ADR-0027 §2 (what a recorded review covers), `CLAUDE.md` golden rules 1–4.
**Contradictions against `origin/main`:** none. The standing finding reproduces exactly
as the handoff comment states it, verified against the text before the fix (below).

## The standing finding is fixed, and the fix was verified against the bug

`benchmarks/memory/run.py:348` derived a case's store directory as
`case.case_key.replace("/", "_")`, which is not injective: `"a/b"` and `"a_b"` both named
`cases/a_b`. Two cases in one directory share `memory.db`, `conversations.db` and
`deferrals.db`, so one case's beliefs can answer another's questions — the property
`execute_run`'s own docstring claims.

- **`case_dir_name`** names the directory as a sanitised prefix of the key plus a
  12-hex-character digest of the *whole* key. The prefix keeps `--keep-stores` output
  recognisable, which is the only reason that flag exists; the digest is what makes the
  mapping injective. A bare digest was rejected for the same reason.
- **`plan_run` refuses duplicate `case_key`s.** No naming scheme separates a key from
  itself, and both CLI commands plan before they run, so this is caught before a store
  is opened or a model call is made.
- **Tests.** An end-to-end run over `"a/b"` and `"a_b"` under `--keep-stores` asserting
  two distinct directories, a `memory.db` in each, and disjoint retrieved-id sets per
  case; a unit check on the naming; and the `plan_run` duplicate refusal.
- **The test was checked against the defect, not only against the fix.** Reverting the
  one line to the old mapping fails `test_colliding_keys_get_their_own_stores`
  (`assert {'a_b'} == {'a_b-648fa9b31bc7', 'a_b-c14cddc033f6'}`) plus the two existing
  directory-naming tests, then passes again when restored. The fake observer derives
  record ids from content, so the two fixture cases carry disjoint content — identical
  content would have produced identical ids in separate stores and made the disjointness
  assertion vacuous.

Neither shipped corpus reaches the defect (LoCoMo `conv-26 … conv-50`, LongMemEval
`gpt4_…`/`…_abs` — no slashes, no duplicates); `read_slice` over a hand-written slice and
`stratified` over a list with duplicates do.

---

## Pre-flight (predecessor's, written before any code, against `origin/main` @ `6bee9973`)

**Will touch:** `benchmarks/**` (new), `tests/benchmarks/**` (new), `pyproject.toml` (mypy `files`, pytest `pythonpath`).
**Will not touch:** `src/ai_assistant/**`, `docs/adr/**`, `docs/roadmap.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`, `.github/**`.
**Governing:** ADR-0006/0024 (embedder), ADR-0042 (composition root), ADR-0074/0075 (capture), ADR-0077 (observation), ADR-0072/0113/0128 (retrieval), ADR-0119 (traces, correlation), ADR-0136 (gate cadence), golden rules 1–4.
**No ADR is written.** The brief names offline dev tooling as the precedent; the precedent it names (`ai-assistant-measures`) does not hold — that lives *inside* `src/` and is ratified by ADR-0120 §9. The precedent that does hold is `scripts/`: a top-level tree outside `src/`, added to mypy's `files`, driven from the justfile, with no ADR of its own. This harness implements no normative clause and creates no contract, so it takes that shape.

**Three claims in the brief / #1029 that do not survive contact with the tree.** Each is a FLAG, not a STOP — none changes the lane's shape:

1. **"All inference in worker processes, never the hub" names no mechanism that exists.** There is no `multiprocessing`, no process pool and no inference worker anywhere in `src/`. Model inference runs in-process on the hub's event loop (`service/transport.py`, `service/hub.py`: "the **in-process** engine this hub owns"). The nearest real thing is *embedding*, offloaded to bounded daemon **threads** by the private `models/_embed_worker.py` (ADR-0118 §7), which is not shared and has no public surface. The harness satisfies the clause the only way available: it is its own process and never runs inside the hub.
2. **Per-predicate exclusion telemetry exists as keys and is structurally zero as data.** `excluded_kind`, `excluded_retention`, `excluded_window` and `excluded_band` are written as literal `0` by `SqliteMemoryStore`, deliberately: since ADR-0128 §1 every eligibility predicate binds inside the KNN, so no candidate is dropped post-hoc and there is nothing to count. #1029's P8 is unaffected — the split it predicts is computed from the traces' `returned` record-id sets against the corpus's own evidence pointers, which is what the harness records — but a prediction phrased in terms of those four counts would read zeros. Note that `app/composition.py`'s own comment still says those counts are why the emitter sits inside the store; that comment is now stale. Filed rather than fixed (out of fence).
3. **The corpus #1029 names is deprecated by its author.** `xiaowu0162/longmemeval` is marked deprecated upstream and replaced by `longmemeval-cleaned`, which "removes noisy history sessions that interfere with the answer correctness". These are different corpora and do not produce the same scores. The harness defaults to the cleaned variant and keeps the original reachable as a separate corpus key; **the owner decides which the pre-registration is conditioned on before any scored run.**

## Placement: why `benchmarks/` and not `src/ai_assistant/`

This is dev/evaluation tooling, not product code, and the placement is the argument the brief asked for a paragraph on.

Inside `src/ai_assistant` it would be a package every one of the seventeen `lint-imports` contracts has to be taught about by name (each enumerates its sources; the contracts' own comments warn that an unlisted package is one the rules are *asserted about and not checked on*), a package the wheel would carry, and a second composition root sitting beside `app/`. Outside `src/`, it is an ordinary consumer of the published surface: it imports `ai_assistant.*` as an external application would, `hatch`'s explicit `packages = ["src/ai_assistant"]` keeps it out of the wheel, and no architecture contract changes.

The one thing that placement costs is that `[tool.importlinter] root_package = "ai_assistant"` cannot see this tree, so golden rule 4 is not mechanically enforced on it. Extending `root_packages` was tried and rejected: `uv run lint-imports` is a console script whose `sys.path[0]` is the venv's `bin/`, so `benchmarks` is not importable there, and the fix would have to be in the CI workflow — outside this lane's fence. Instead `tests/benchmarks/test_import_discipline.py` parses every module in the tree and fails on a provider-SDK import. Same rule, different mechanism, and it works under bare `pytest` in CI with no workflow change.

**Two `pyproject.toml` entries, both in-fence:** `benchmarks` added to mypy's `files` (the `scripts/` precedent, and it earns it more — this tree imports the package, so a signature change becomes a type error rather than a surprise at the first paid run); and `pythonpath = ["."]` under pytest, without which `import benchmarks` from `tests/benchmarks/` resolves to the *test* directory as a PEP 420 namespace package and the harness is silently untested. No justfile recipe: `python -m benchmarks.memory` is the entry point and adding one bought nothing.

## What the harness does

- **Corpus acquisition is part of the lane and it worked.** Both corpora fetch non-interactively. Every file is pinned twice — to an immutable upstream revision *and* to a SHA-256 — and verification is unconditional, because a corpus that can move underneath a frozen prediction makes "refuted" unreadable. Provenance, licences and citations live in `benchmarks/memory/corpora/provenance.py`. **LoCoMo is CC BY-NC 4.0 (non-commercial, attribution)**; LongMemEval is MIT. Nothing is committed; the cache is git-ignored.
- **Ingestion is the real pipeline, minus the half it must not use.** Not `Engine.converse`: that asks a model to plan and answer *every turn*, which would discard the corpus's own assistant side (where much of LongMemEval's evidence lives — #1029's P6) and cost two model calls per turn across ~5,900 turns. So the harness wires the same public classes `app/composition.py` wires — `SqliteMemoryStore`, the settings-selected `BoundedEmbedder`, `ConversationLifecycle.capture`, `ModelBackedObserver`, `DefaultMemoryPolicy`, `MemoryIngestor`, `MemoryWriteStage`, `SqliteTraceStore` — and imports `RETRIEVAL_LIMIT`/`CONFLICT_LIMIT` from the composition root rather than copying them, so it cannot silently measure a budget the product does not use.
- **The cadence is interleaved because `ObservationStage` reads a window, not a cursor** (the reason ADR-0083 §13 ships the observation job disabled). Capture a batch, observe it, capture the next: the windows tile and every turn is read exactly once.
- **Runs on the corpus's clock.** LoCoMo spans 293 days; LongMemEval haystacks span months and then ask "which did I do first?". Capturing at `datetime.now()` collapses that span silently and deletes the axis P2 is entirely about. One `BenchmarkClock` is injected into capture, the store's liveness axes, the ingestor and the observer; the trace clock stays on the wall, which is the separation ADR-0119 §5 exists for.
- **Answering reads retrieved context and nothing else**, by construction rather than by prompt wording — `assemble_by_band` with `BELIEF_KINDS`, then `ModelProvider.complete`. Golden rule 4 holds here too: no provider SDK anywhere in the tree.
- **P4 and P8 come from ADR-0119, not from bookkeeping.** Each question runs inside a `correlated_operation()` scope, so every `RETRIEVAL` trace underneath carries its id; the harness reads them back and records `search_calls`, the returned record-id sets, `limit`/`fetch_k`/`candidates`/`bands`, and outcomes. `fetch_k < limit` is recorded as `ceiling_bound` — the offline reading of `MemorySearchResult.capped`, since the trace carries no `capped` key.
- **Two graders.** `ExactGrader` makes no model call and is the default (and what the tests use); `ModelGrader` is the LLM judge both benchmarks' published protocols use, and is what a scored run would need for comparability.
- **`plan` costs nothing and is the command to run before spending.** Real output, this branch, full LoCoMo:

  ```
  cases (one store each)          10
  questions                       1,986
  turns captured                  3,075
  observation model calls         157
  answering model calls           1,986
  judging model calls (at most)   1,540
  total model calls (at most)     3,683
  ```

  It also warns, correctly, that the default 30-day `episode_retention` against a 293-day case expires early sessions' episodes before late ones are captured under the corpus clock — set `ASSISTANT_EPISODE_RETENTION=none` for a real run. **This is a number #1029's budget should be re-read against**: 3,683 sequential calls at standard pricing is not the ~$10 the batched estimate assumed, and #1034 already rules the pilot runs sequentially.

## Review

**Adversarial, twelve rounds. Rounds 1–7 were the predecessor's; 8–12 are the
successor's**, run under the ADR-0138 §1 handoff comment on this PR. Rounds 1–7 held every
finding and waived none. Round 8 raised one `blocker` (**#1052**). Round 9, against the
settled floor, raised three — one **fixed** (#1064), one filed (#1065), one rebutted.
Round 10 raised three — a rediscovery of #1052, one **fixed** (#1069), one filed (#1070).
Round 11 raised three — one **fixed** (the observation-cadence defect below), one cited to
#1052, one parked as #1074.

**Three of my five rounds ended in a waiver the coordinator overturned or a STOP, and each
overturn was right.** The rule that settled all of them: `CLAUDE.md`'s triage carves by
**severity and in-diff-ness**, not by how bad the consequence feels — a defect writing
false provenance, a command that can hang, and an episode silently dropped from a case's
memory are one category, and the last of them would never have been reached if the first
waiver had stood.

Every waiver's rationale is recorded below, and every deferral has an issue, which is what
makes the lens terminal under ADR-0138 §3. Twenty-one findings were fixed across the
twelve rounds.

| round | verdict | findings | what they were about |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | APPROVE WITH NITS | 2 major, 1 minor | judge failure ended the run; scored run over a truncated history; negative `--limit` |
| 2 | APPROVE WITH NITS | 3 major | a failed answer discarded telemetry it had already produced; scored run defaulted to the exact grader; scored run allowed the hashing embedder |
| 3 | BLOCK | 1 blocker, 2 major | the gate was only at the command line; a judge verdict matched by prefix; concurrent fetches shared one staging path |
| 4 | BLOCK | 1 blocker, 1 major, 1 minor | the judge was classified by display name and injected seams were accepted for a scored run; negative `--limit` on the LongMemEval arm; a rejected URL left a staging file |
| 5 | BLOCK | 1 blocker, 1 major | `RunMode` is a `StrEnum`, so the gate's identity test returned early on the bare string `"scored"`; credentials unchecked when only the judge was real |
| 6 | BLOCK | 1 blocker, 1 major | `preregistration_final="false"` read as confirmation; credential check refused fallback routes the harness never builds |
| 7 | APPROVE WITH NITS | 1 major | distinct case keys can map to one store directory — **fixed, above** |
| 8 | BLOCK | 1 blocker | the scored-run gate trusts a caller-declared `max_sessions` — **waived, #1052** |
| 9 | BLOCK | 1 blocker, 2 major | fresh session against the settled floor; two waived (**#1065**, one rebutted), one **fixed** after the coordinator overturned its waiver (#1064) |
| 10 | BLOCK | 1 blocker, 1 major, 1 minor | fresh session on the fix; the `blocker` is #1052 rediscovered, the `minor` filed as **#1070**, the `major` **fixed** after its waiver was overturned (#1069) |
| 11 | APPROVE WITH NITS | 3 major | one **fixed** (the observation-cadence defect, below), one cited to #1052, one parked as **#1074** |
| 12 | APPROVE WITH NITS | 2 major, 1 minor | **terminal** — both majors are rediscoveries of #1074 and #1052; the `minor` filed as **#1080** |

Churn ratio was 1.0–1.1 throughout and never approached ADR-0138 §1's 1.5 arm; at round 10
it printed 1.1 as a lower bound, 6,482 lines touched ÷ 5,904 net.

**Every finding across all ten rounds was verified against the actual text before acting,
and every one held on its mechanism.** Eighteen were fixed. Two of the last six were
rebutted on their reasoning rather than their facts, and each rebuttal is written out
below rather than asserted.

### Waived `blocker` — round 8, `benchmarks/memory/run.py`, filed as #1052

> The scored-run gate trusts the caller-supplied `max_sessions` metadata rather than the
> cases in `plan`. A direct API caller can `plan_run(corpus, first_sessions(cases, 2), …)`
> and then `execute_run(…, mode=SCORED, max_sessions=0, preregistration_final=True)`: the
> gate permits it and the manifest claims whole histories, but every answer was produced
> from truncated history.

**The mechanism is real and I verified it** — `first_sessions` truncates in the selection
layer before `plan_run`, and `execute_run` takes the bound as a parameter it both records
and gates on. Waived rather than fixed, on four grounds:

1. **Unreachable while #1029 ground rule 1 stands.** Every scored run is refused without
   an explicit operator statement that the pre-registration is final. None has been made
   and no scored run has been executed.
2. **The CLI cannot produce the inconsistency.** `_select` feeds one `max_sessions`
   variable to both `first_sessions` and `execute_run`, so the shortening and the
   declaration are the same number by construction.
3. **The finding's framing overstates one point.** It says this contradicts a documented
   claim that direct callers cannot skip the gate. `refuse_ineligible_scored_run`'s
   docstring documents the opposite for this very clause: the injected-seams check "is
   also the only one of the five that can be checked without trusting anything a caller
   says". The defect holds; the contradiction does not.
4. **The fix is a design change, not a guard.** Binding selection provenance onto
   `RunPlan` — or moving selection inside the execution boundary — reshapes the seam
   between `select.py`, `plan_run` and `execute_run`. That belongs in its own lane, and
   #1052 records it as a hard precondition on the first scored run rather than as a nice
   to have.

### The base move that cost round 9, and the round that answered it

Round 8 was recorded against base `6eb04080dd14`. `main` then moved to `78e50af2cb3e` as
five lanes landed, and `scripts/ship.sh --drill` on the rebased head reported the breach
that costs a round:

```
  base move             6eb04080dd14..78e50af2cb3e
    files examined      45
      [FLOOR] A docs/adr/0141-…md
      [FLOOR] A docs/adr/0143-…md
      [FLOOR] M src/ai_assistant/core/protocols.py
      [FLOOR] M src/ai_assistant/core/types.py
    §3 floor            BREACHED by the marked path(s) — this base move
                        costs a review round.
    §2(b) verdict       unavailable — floor breach (§3)
```

That round was authorised by the coordinator once the floor had settled — no
floor-touching lane is open — and spent as round 9, against base `78e50af2cb3e`. It ran
as a **fresh session** rather than a resumed one, so it re-read the whole diff from
scratch; that is why its three findings are all new ground rather than continuations.

### Waived round-9 findings, with the rationale for each

**1. `blocker` — "the harness is a second composition root outside `app/`."** Waived, and
this one is **rebutted on the merits**. `benchmarks/` is outside the `ai_assistant`
package entirely — `[tool.importlinter] root_package = "ai_assistant"` cannot reach it —
so it is an external consumer of the published surface exactly as `tests/` is, and the
test suite wires concretes on every integration test without that being a boundary
breach. Golden rule 1 forbids one *subsystem* importing another's concrete module; it does
not route every consumer through `app/`. The direction the finding proposes — an
ADR-backed public composition surface shaped for this benchmark — would move a benchmark
concern into the product's public API, which is the worse trade, and it is a `src/` plus
`docs/adr/**` change this lane's fence excludes outright. The one piece of residue worth
keeping is that `lint-imports` does not cover this tree, which the PR already mitigates
with `tests/benchmarks/test_import_discipline.py` and which is now **#1065**.

**2. `major` — "`longmemeval-original` runs write records labelled `longmemeval`."**
**Fixed — this waiver was overturned by the coordinator and the fix is in the diff.**
`Fixes #1064`. The finding was correct: `_select` routes both keys through one loader
which hard-coded `corpus_key="longmemeval"`, so a run of the original variant produced a
manifest naming the original beside a `records.jsonl` whose every row named the cleaned
corpus — two artifacts of one run disagreeing about which corpus produced them, and they
are corpora that do not produce the same scores.

`longmemeval.load` now takes `corpus_key` as a **required keyword with no default**, and
`_select` passes `corpus.key`. The absence of a default is the fix, not an accident:
provenance that can be defaulted is provenance that gets assumed, which is precisely how
this was written the first time. Pinned by
`test_longmemeval_carries_the_corpus_it_was_told_it_is_reading`, which loads one file
under both keys and asserts the cases carry each.

The waiver was wrong and the overturn was right: `CLAUDE.md`'s triage rule — blocker/major
**and** about code in the diff → fix it now — outranks an edit budget, which exists to
stop churn rather than to ship a verified defect with a one-parameter fix.

**3. `major` — "the plan overstates model costs by counting judge calls the default
exact grader will not make."** Waived, and **rebutted**: the field is documented as an
upper bound (`judge_calls`: "Model calls grading would make, **at most**") and the CLI
prints it as one twice — `judging model calls (at most)` and `total model calls (at
most)`. The `plan` command exists to budget the run #1029 pays for, and a scored run
*must* use the model judge (the gate refuses any other), so for the run being budgeted
the figure is exact rather than inflated.

### Round-10 findings

Round 10 ran on the #1064 fix, again as a fresh session.

**1. `blocker` — the scored-run gate trusts a caller-declared `max_sessions`.** This is
**#1052 rediscovered**, independently, by a reviewer with no memory of round 8. Same
mechanism, same rationale, same waiver — which stands as recorded and as the coordinator
has confirmed. The rediscovery corroborates the finding; it adds nothing to it.

**2. `major` — corpus downloads have no timeout.** **Fixed — this waiver was overturned
too, and on the argument I had made against myself.** `Fixes #1069`. Verified:
`urllib.request.urlopen` was called with no per-call timeout, so it inherited the global
socket default of `None`, and a peer that completes the TLS handshake then sends nothing
left `fetch` — and `run`, which fetches on the way in — blocked forever.

`_download` now passes an explicit timeout. **It is a per-operation bound, not a cap on
the transfer**, and that distinction is what makes a number safe: the largest pinned
artifact is 2.7 GiB, so a limit on how long a download may take would refuse a slow but
healthy connection, where a limit on how long the socket may deliver *nothing* refuses
only a dead one. Nothing else was needed — `TimeoutError` is an `OSError`, so the handler
already in that function removes the partial file and raises `CorpusFetchError` with the
stall preserved as the cause. `test_a_stalled_transfer_fails_instead_of_hanging` drives
that path and asserts the bound is passed and finite; removing the keyword fails it on
`isinstance(None, float)`.

I had waived it on the ground that it touches no artifact. The overturn is right and the
reason generalises: **the triage rule carves by severity and in-diff-ness, not by
consequence class**, and inventing a per-finding exception for "this one only wastes an
operator's afternoon" is how the rule stops meaning anything.

**3. `minor` — a malformed cache entry escapes as a raw OS error.** Filed as **#1070**,
which is where `CLAUDE.md`'s triage sends anything below blocker/major. Verified: a cache
path that is a directory satisfies `target.exists()` and makes `digest_of` raise
`IsADirectoryError` from outside any handler, where `ensure_file` documents
`CorpusFetchError`.

### Round 11 — and the defect that was worth all of this

Round 11 returned `APPROVE WITH NITS` with three `major`s, on a fresh session again.

**1. `major` — a degraded capture could cost the episode before it its observation.
Fixed.** This is the one that justifies the last four rounds, and it was silent.

`ConversationLifecycle.capture` appends the index entry **first** and writes the episode
**second**, so an episode-stage failure — or ADR-0074 §8's compensation deleting a
just-written episode — leaves a turn standing in the conversation whose episode id no
longer resolves. `ObservationStage._select` reads `turns(conversation_id,
limit=batch_size)` — the most recent N **turns** — and skips an unresolvable one
**without backfilling**, deliberately: *"Backfilling would make the window's span depend
on how many gaps it contains."* So that turn **holds a slot**.

The driver paced observation on *successful* captures. At a batch of two, success →
degrade → success observed the window `[degraded, second]`, and the first episode fell
out of every window that would ever be read. Never distilled, with nothing reporting it:
the case's memory is simply missing an episode, which biases the retrieval this pilot
exists to measure. The regression test shows it is worse than the finding claimed —
under the old cadence **both** episodes before the gap were lost, and the only content the
observer ever saw was `Ada: Juno is settling in.`

Every capture now counts toward the batch and is classified afterwards. A lost *append*
records no turn and holds no slot, but `CaptureReport` reports both failures identically,
so the driver cannot tell them apart and takes the safe direction: `batch_size` is
documented as *"a maximum, not a quota"*, so over-counting under-fills a window where
under-counting drops episodes. **That indistinguishability is a real contract question and
is filed as #1075** against orchestration's surface, referenced from the fix's comment
rather than folded in here.

**2. `major` — `corpus_digests` is unvalidated for a scored run.** Correct, and **not a
new finding**: it is #1052, whose text already generalises to "any other precondition that
is metadata about the data rather than about the configuration". Cited, not re-filed.

**3. `major` — P8's retrieved-vs-not split has no join.** Correct, and **parked as
#1074**. Corpus evidence pointers (`D1:1`) and `retrieved_ids` (generated record ids) are
different id spaces with no retained mapping, and the default cleanup removes the stores
that would carry one. It is a question about #1029's *analysis design*, not about code
behaviour, and #1029 is the owner's to edit.

### Round 12 — terminal

Nothing new that this PR must fix, which is what ends the lens under ADR-0138 §3.

- **`major` — P8's split has no join.** #1074, rediscovered. Cited.
- **`major` — `corpus_digests` unvalidated for a scored run.** #1052, rediscovered a third
  time across three independent sessions. Cited. Its recurrence is itself worth reading:
  the reviewer keeps arriving at the same seam from different directions, which is the
  argument for closing #1052 before the first scored run rather than at leisure.
- **`minor` — `plan` is documented as contacting nothing but fetches on a cold cache.**
  Correct, and filed as **#1080**. Two loose statements describe the *command*
  (`README.md:44`, `__main__.py:14`); the two precise ones describing `plan_run` itself
  ("contacts no provider and opens no store") are accurate and should survive the fix.
  Routed out by the triage rule rather than waived.

**Issues filed across both holders: #1052, #1053, #1065, #1070, #1074, #1075, #1080** —
and
**#1064 and #1069, which this PR closes**. #1053 is the `app/composition.py`
`RETRIEVAL`-emitter comment that still cites the per-predicate exclusion counts ADR-0128
§1 made structurally zero — the pre-flight's point 2, out of this lane's fence.

Three of the sixteen were `minor` and were fixed rather than filed as issues, against
`CLAUDE.md`'s default. Each was a two-to-three-line guard in a file this PR creates, and
each closed an asymmetry the same PR had introduced — a negative `--limit` accepted on
one selector while its sibling refused it, and a staging file leaked by lines added one
round earlier. Fixing them grew the PR by less than filing them would have cost to
carry.

### A live smoke run was executed, and it is not a measurement

Three questions, two LoCoMo sessions, the **real** on-device embedder
(`BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5@d43150a691d02e46+9c016380489105f7`) and the **real** Anthropic
route through the `ModelProvider` seam — four model calls in total. It exercised the two
paths no test can: the FastEmbed embedder and a live provider. It proved capture (18
turns), distillation (1 observation pass, 4 proposals), retrieval (3 band-scoped `search`
calls, correlation-linked), and that `traces.db` survives while the other stores are
removed.

**It is a smoke run under #1029's ground rule 1 and its outputs have not been read as
scores.** Its manifest says `"mode": "smoke"`. Its artifacts are under `benchmarks/.runs/`,
which git ignores, and nothing from it is in this diff.

items.title: Simplify and rank benchmarks
items.body:
## What changed

- replace the Core/Extended split with one unified seven-challenge benchmark catalog
- remove the suite toggle, `u` hotkey, suite state, suite metadata, and difficulty suffixes from terminal task names
- rename the destructive full-catalog action to **Run All** and retain its exact turn count plus two-step confirmation
- anchor the previous/next selector buttons around a responsive cell sized for the longest challenge name, keeping render and click coordinates stable as selection changes
- add a sortable overall `RANK` column for each model/reasoning-effort combination
- add responsive, clickable Cost/Balanced/Speed weighting controls plus a `w` cycling hotkey; changing them recomputes existing ranks immediately
- compute ranking once per render and reuse it for display and Rank sorting; column sizing derives its maximum label from the distinct model/effort combinations without ranking the results
- move Easy/Moderate/Hard guidance into one README challenge table and document the ranking algorithm and measurement caveats
- bump the maintained minor version from `0.4.0` to `0.5.0`

## Ranking

Ranking aggregates every completed result row for a model/reasoning-effort combination. More passes dominate, followed by fewer failures. Within each identical pass/failure tier, Codexometer independently ranks total API-equivalent cost and total wall time, then combines the two ordinal ranks at 75/25 for Cost mode, 50/50 for Balanced, or 25/75 for Speed. This tier isolation prevents a failing combination from changing the efficiency trade-off between fully correct peers. Token usage remains visible but no longer affects rank. Missing or invalid cost receives the last cost-axis rank in its correctness tier rather than appearing artificially cheap; exact weighted-score ties share a rank, and ranks are provisional while results are still arriving.

The README now specifies the grouping key, aggregation and validation rules, competition ranking, exact formulas (`3C + T`, `C + T`, and `C + 3T`), final correctness-first comparison, missing-cost consequences, token independence, and provisional in-progress behavior.

## Why

The suite split consumed control space and added selection state without changing how an individual challenge was evaluated. A single catalog makes challenge navigation and full runs easier to understand. Compact terminal names reclaim room for ranking, while difficulty remains available where its meaning can be properly explained.

The anchored selector prevents the arrow controls and their mouse hit targets from shifting when task-name lengths differ.

## Validation

- `go test ./...`
- `go test -race -cover ./...`
- `go vet ./...`
- rebuilt the local binary and Darwin, Linux, and Windows distributions for amd64 and arm64
- regression coverage for unified ordering/names, exact Run All turn/task selection, stable selector coordinates and hit testing, correctness precedence and tier isolation, independent cost/time ranks, all three weighting modes, token independence, displayed-order hotkey cycling, immediate mouse/hotkey recomputation, responsive click surfaces, rank sorting, incomplete measurements, and exact ties
- regression coverage that Rank sorting reuses the supplied, mode-specific ranking map
- confirmed the rebuilt local binary reports `codexometer v0.5.0`

items.body:
## Summary Measure the current monolithic outbox-state write amplification through public APIs and record an evidence-backed `migration-plan-required` decision without changing production persistence. Closes #14. ## Changed - Add a release-mode `SyncStoreBenchmark` executable depending only on `HealthRelayCore`. - Stage deterministic empty synthetic records for 30, 90, 365, and 1,825 days through `FileSyncStore.stageDaily`. - Run three isolated trials per range and report invariant CSV medians for elapsed time, final state bytes, and cumulative state bytes. - Buffer all output and sanitize failures so benchmark errors cannot leak temporary paths or identifiers. - Record two raw benchmark samples, scaling ratios, alternatives, the preferred file-based v2 investigation, and mandatory rollback/migration constraints. - Leave `FileSyncStore` and every production schema unchanged. ## Review aids ```mermaid flowchart LR B["Stage N synthetic days"] --> J["Rewrite monolithic JSON each day"] J --> F["Final size grows linearly
~1,265 bytes/day"] J --> C["Cumulative writes grow quadratically
2.11 GB at 1,825 days"] C --> D["Decision: migration plan required"] D --> V2["Investigate file-based v2
small metadata index + split bulk bytes"] ``` Representative medians: | Days | Elapsed run 1 | Elapsed run 2 | Final state | Cumulative writes | |---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 30 | 14.733 ms | 15.261 ms | 38,027 B | 590,535 B | | 365 | 657.795 ms | 640.246 ms | 461,802 B | 84,523,780 B | | 1,825 | 14,048.977 ms | 14,176.319 ms | 2,308,702 B | 2,107,915,150 B | ## Risks - Results characterize one sanitized Apple Silicon environment and establish a scaling curve, not a universal latency threshold. - The benchmark uses empty synthetic records; real encoded content may increase state size and rewrite volume. - This PR deliberately stops at a decision. A separate reviewed plan must define v2 storage, compatibility, recovery, and migration before production edits. ## Verification - Release benchmark run twice — exact byte results reproduced; elapsed variance at most 7.9%. - Comma-decimal locale release run — preserved one header and four four-field CSV rows. - `make test-core` — 64 tests passed. - `make verify` after final corrections — passed. - Production `FileSyncStore.swift` branch diff — empty. - `$autoreview` first pass found locale-dependent CSV and unsanitized failure output; both were corrected. - `$autoreview` second pass — clean, 0.98 correctness score. ## Complexity Medium. The executable is isolated and deterministic; the substantive outcome is an explicit migration-planning boundary backed by reproducible measurements.

## Summary

The benchmark & KPI framework (Phase 1, per `docs/spec/benchmark/` — architecture, corpus, KPI catalog) plus the first published 8-model baseline.

## Proposal (signed off)

Benchmark scoring redesign + the quality-perception corpus (from the review: correctness/robustness saturation made the old score rank models on ~6 scenarios plus single-run noise).

**Part 1 — scoring:**
- `total = 0.40·correctness + 0.25·efficiency + 0.20·agentic + 0.10·robustness + 0.05·adherence` — agentic (tool economy, the only lens with real spread: mean 64.8 vs total 86.4) enters the score; saturated sub-scores demoted.
- correctness now uses `arg_precision` — the partial-credit signal the oracle computed and the score ignored.
- Failed scenarios: `total *= 0.5` → `min(total, 60)` — honest partial credit, no more 49-point "failures".

**Part 2 — `checks_weight` knob:** per-scenario (default 0.2 = v2 formula exactly); review scenarios set 0.8 so issue checks dominate the single read-step bullseye.

**Part 3 — quality-perception suite (Phase A):** 12 scenarios, 2 per category (system architecture, refactoring, code quality, data structures, design patterns, clean code), each pair with a clean-code **control** (correct answer: "nothing major" — calibrates over-eager critics). ## Summary

Verified `ConceptSeparabilityBenchmark`'s hand-rolled silhouette score and nearest-centroid linear-probe accuracy against sklearn on synthetic fixtures, per the issue's acceptance criteria.
One unintentional divergence found and fixed; no divergence in the linear probe.

**Silhouette score for a singleton cluster**: the implementation set `a(i)=0` (no other same-cluster member to average) and ran that through the general formula `s(i) = (b(i)-a(i))/max(a(i),b(i))`, producing `1.0` — "perfectly separated" — for a cluster whose separation quality can't actually be assessed.
`sklearn.metrics.silhouette_samples`'s source comments this exact case: `# nan values are for clusters of size 1, and should be 0`, matching Rousseeuw's original 1987 definition (a(i) undefined → whole score defined as 0, not derived from the general formula).
Fixed to match: a singleton cluster's sample now scores `0.0` directly.

Practical impact is low — the benchmark's default `probe_reps=3` gives every class the same sample count, so a singleton cluster can't occur in a normal run, and no benchmark conclusion depended on this path.
Fixed anyway since the cost was trivial and this is exactly the kind of latent divergence the issue was opened to catch.

items.title: Add benchmark evaluation and scoring engine

labels.name: testing
labels.description: Test coverage, validation, determinism, and quality assurance

labels.name: benchmark
labels.description: Benchmark datasets, evaluation contracts, metrics, and scoring evidence

items.body:
Adds a deterministic evaluation layer that scores an agent's predictions against the emitted observed state. It computes **evidence, not opinion**: no scoring weights, no readiness index, no composite score.

Closes #9

## Prediction contract

One versioned JSONL file (`schema_version: 1`), deliberately small — an agent supplies only what it could know from the observed graph, never ground-truth-only fields. Three distinct claims: `finding`, explicit `clean`, and `abstain`, so silence and refusal are never conflated. An optional remediation object carries `action_class`, `availability`, `approval_policy`, `approver_role` and `recommended_value`, keeping availability and approval as the independent axes issue #8 established.

Validation is **total**: the whole file is inspected before anything is raised, and nothing is silently dropped. Malformed JSON, unsupported schema versions, duplicate ids and pairs, unknown entity/rule ids, invalid enums, non-finite or out-of-range confidence, and contradictory remediation fields are each rejected with the line, field, value and expected contract.

## Evaluation universe

Pair-level on `(entity_id, rule_id)`, with each rule's population read from `rule-scope.jsonl`:

- population = `eligible_ids ∪ control_excluded_ids`
- positives = `selected_ids`
- negatives = eligible-unselected plus reserved controls

Entities that were never in a rule's population are **not** negatives for it. Pairing every rule with every entity would manufacture tens of thousands of free true negatives and push specificity towards 1.0 for any agent; a `never-eligible` control is known to the benchmark and enters no denominator.

## Finding metrics

TP/FP/FN/TN, precision, recall, specificity, F1, FPR and FNR — every one derived from counts, never from other metrics, with F1 computed as `2TP/(2TP+FP+FN)` so it stays defined when precision is not. Micro (sum cells, divide once) and macro (unweighted mean of *defined* per-rule values, with `group_count`/`total_groups` recorded). Breakdowns by rule, category, severity, entity kind, entity class, and control partition; each partitions the same pairs and sums to the overall matrix.

**Undefined metrics are `null`** with their numerator and denominator, never `0.0`. Precision with no predicted positives is a question that was never asked; a zero there misdescribes a silent agent and drags every average down with a number nobody measured.

## Remediation metrics

Scored only against correctly detected findings. Field-level correctness for availability, approval policy, approver role, action class and recommended value, plus `fully_correct`. Three rates keep detection and repair from being confounded: coverage, correctness-given-a-true-positive, and end-to-end. A correct non-remediable result is an explicit `no-remediation` **decision** — omitting it scores `missing`, not correct. A finding that was never detected is reported as `unscored-missed-finding` rather than re-charged as a remediation error.

## Reserved controls and out-of-scope predictions

Reserved controls are legitimate negatives *and* are broken out separately — a false positive there is a distinct, more serious failure. An actionable fix proposed against any clean entity is flagged `unsafe_action` (with `unsafe_on_reserved_control` where it applies): a detection error stays on paper, but an accompanying remediation would have altered a correct record.

Predictions naming a known entity outside a rule's population are reported as `out_of_scope_false_positive`, counted in a strict false-positive total, and excluded from every denominator. Predictions naming no rule are never guessed into a pair; they are scored in entity-level and category-level universes derived the same way from the rule scopes.

## Determinism

Canonical JSON, records sorted by id, no wall-clock anywhere, no reliance on dict or set iteration order. Each summary records the ground-truth fingerprint, the prediction SHA-256, and the evaluator/schema versions. Verified byte-identical across repeat runs, across processes and across `PYTHONHASHSEED` values.

## CLI

```bash
dataswamp evaluate --observed-dir generated/observed --predictions predictions.jsonl --output-dir generated/evaluation
```

Ground truth and the submission are fully validated before anything is written, so an invalid submission never replaces a previous evaluation. Uses the issue #3 containment guard, extended to protect the observed directory and the prediction file; `--force` overrides only the non-empty check, never path safety. Exit codes 0/1/2 follow the existing convention.

Outputs: `evaluation-summary.json`, `finding-results.jsonl`, `remediation-results.jsonl`, `rule-metrics.jsonl`, `category-metrics.jsonl`, `evaluation-report.md`, `provenance.json`.

## Tests

89 new tests (514 → 516 total, 1 expected skip). A hand-built four-rule ground truth pins every confusion-matrix cell exactly; the canonical scenario's real observed state proves the degenerate strategies score correctly (perfect → 1.0; empty → 0 recall, full specificity, *undefined* precision; flag-everything → full recall, zero specificity, precision < 0.05). Three small committed fixtures cover every remediation contract state, an unsafe action on a reserved control, and a missing no-remediation decision.

## Compatibility

The evaluator is strictly read-only with respect to every other layer. The issue #2 control partition, issue #3 output safety, issue #4 provenance contract and issue #8 rule/remediation contract are untouched, and the committed golden digests are unchanged — that they still match is itself the compatibility assertion.

## Known limitations

- No fuzzy or semantic matching; `rule_id` is matched exactly, by design for this milestone.
- Confidence is summarised shallowly (count, mean, min, max). No calibration, no ROC/AUC — that would be a modelling claim out of scope here.
- `finding-results.jsonl` omits true-negative pairs that carry no prediction; the summary counts always cover the full universe.
- No baseline agent implementation, per the issue's scope boundaries.

items.title: feat(benchmark): leaderboard artifacts as spec-conformant EvalScoreRecords (#9265)
items.body:
> **Stacked** on #9600 (stack #9601): #9595 → #9598 → #9599 → #9600 → this.

## What

#9216 requirement 5 is explicit that leaderboard artifacts are **exactly** the eval-interface's consumable score records — no parallel format. So this emits `EvalScoreRecord`s with `workUnit.kind === "benchmark_run"` through the same `contentDigest` path the `outcome_confirmed_precision` records already use, and derives the board from those records and **nothing else**.

That last point is the structural one: there is no second query path from the scorer to the board. A number on the leaderboard is, by construction, a field of a record a third party can fetch, re-derive and digest-verify — so the published board and the consumable feed cannot disagree, because they're the same data read twice.

## Two policies enforced here rather than left to a caller's discipline

**Held-out cadence (#9263 decision 2).** The emitter is the last point before a number becomes public, so it's where cadence is enforced. A held-out record is simply **not built** while the window is open — not built-and-filtered, not built-with-a-flag — so there is no in-memory held-out record for a downstream bug to serialize. The regression test probes this with the would-be record's own **digest**, a 64-hex value unique to that exact content, because my first attempt used the held-out precision as the probe and it was `0` — a substring of almost any JSON, so it passed for the wrong reason.

**Trust tier from the actual execution.** `attested` requires a real envelope; absent one the tier is `reproducible`, never optimistically upgraded. The record type's discriminated union already makes "attested without an envelope" unrepresentable, and the tier sits inside the digest preimage, so a tier claim can't be edited after issuance (asserted: the two tiers produce different digests for otherwise-identical content).

## Score mapping and ranking

The score block maps the multi-class report onto the spec's fixed fields without inventing any: `precision`/`recall` are #9262's **macro** headline, `decided`/`abstained`/`coverage` come from the report's own coverage block, and `confirmed` is the count of decided units the agent got right. Ranking is macro precision descending with **null last** (unmeasurable is not zero, and sorting it as 0 would invent a claim), ties broken by coverage descending then by the earlier `issuedAt`. Immutability is respected rather than worked around: several records for one subject resolve to the latest `issuedAt`, because a corrected score is a new record, never a mutation.

## Tests (14, 100% of branches)

Spec conformance including an exact top-level key set (no extra fields); full commitments block with no placeholders; the score mapping; the decided-nothing null arms; both trust tiers with distinct digests; the not-built-while-open regression; publication at close and on a cadence boundary but not a day either side; the ranking comparator across every arm (null-vs-null falling through to coverage, the `?? -1` fallback from both argument positions, the earlier-claim tiebreak, order-independence); the corrected-score regression; cross-benchmark and cross-kind exclusion; and the empty set.

Also registers the module in `check-dead-source-files`' staged-ahead allowlist — the emitter lands before its serving route (#9216's endpoint sub-issue) and before #9264 supplies the envelopes its `attested` tier consumes, so the checker's flag was correct and the entry names both, as the checker itself instructs.

Closes #9265

items.title: fix(benchmark): Ollama-backed QA harness + correct Recall@k scoring, retract prior figures
items.body:
Two related pieces of benchmark work. Refs #47.

## 1. QA harness runs on local Ollama (`qwen3.5:cloud`)

`BENCHMARK_PLAN.md` already documented an Ollama path, but the code hardcoded `api.openai.com` and threw without `OPENAI_API_KEY`. Now real, and the default: `BENCHMARK_LIMIT=10 npm run benchmark:longmemeval-qa` costs $0 and needs no key. New `benchmarks/lib/llm.ts` is the single transport for both LLM roles; switching to OpenAI is a base-URL change.

**Comparability is enforced, not trusted.** Only a `gpt-4o*` judge follows the paper protocol. With any other judge the runner warns, the report replaces "directly comparable to leaderboard entries" with an explicit not-comparable notice, and every manifest records `judgeModel` + `paperProtocolJudge`. Previously that claim was emitted unconditionally — switching the default would have auto-generated false credibility.

Also fixes **21 pre-existing type errors** that made the QA harness uncompilable despite being marked "✅ Implemented" — it cannot ever have run. Notably `ingest.ts` declared `allSessions` inside the per-instance loop and read it after (a runtime `ReferenceError`), and the scripts referenced `config.limit/offset/cleanup`, which don't exist. Adds a request timeout; there was none, so one stalled call could hang a 500-question run.

## 2. Recall@k was miscomputed — figures retracted

`evaluate.ts` called `recallAtK(ids, answers, ids.length)`. Passing the array's own length as `k` meant `slice(0, k)` never truncated: **R@1, R@3, R@5 and R@10 were all the same number**, computed over the entire retrieved set.

Not marginal — consolidation packs many sessions per row, so "top 5 rows" can hold hundreds of sessions. The published `93.2% R@5` actually meant *"a gold session appeared anywhere among all sessions inside the top 5 rows."*

The surrounding comment shows `k` was disabled **deliberately** — the author treated `k` as rows, not sessions. That's a definitional divergence from LongMemEval, so the fix is definitional:

| Metric | Meaning | Use |
|---|---|---|
| `recallAtKSessions` | gold session among first k distinct sessions by rank | LongMemEval's definition — **headline** |
| `recallAtKRows` | gold session anywhere in top-k rows | MemForge-native, strictly ≥ sessions |

Both are reported with `sessionsPerRow`, so the packing advantage is visible rather than baked into one number. With `CONSOLIDATION_INNER_BATCH_SIZE=1` they converge — asserted in tests.

### Tests where there were none

`tests/benchmark-metrics.test.ts`, 17 tests. The scorer had **zero coverage**, which is how a wrong headline number shipped and survived. The central guard — gold at rank 6 must miss at k=3 — I verified returns `1` under the old implementation and `0` under the new.

### Retraction

Removed from the README badge/status/table, ROADMAP, benchmarks/README, `funding.json` (crawled by funding platforms), and RESULTS.md, which now explains exactly what the number measured. **The PHASE_5_PLAN CI gate enforcing 93.2% is suspended** — a gate defending a retracted number is worse than no gate. Figures return with the corrected re-run.

| Gate | Result |
|---|---|
| benchmarks tsc | 0 errors (was 21) |
| root type-check / lint | clean |
| `test:benchmark-metrics` | 17/17 |
| `test:http` / `integration` / `epistemic-confidence` | 43 / 24 / 33 |
| Ollama judge + reader smoke | verified against live daemon |

Third model measured in the multi-model benchmark, after `luna` run 6 and `glm52`. The run is **complete and scored**; results are appended to `docs/benchmarking-results.md`.

## Result

Rebased to the 97 reachable entries, same scorer and same denominator as the other two rows.

| Metric | `gemini36flash` | `luna` run 6 | `glm52` |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Recall** | **57/97 = 58.8%** | 69/97 = 71.1% | 65/97 = 67.0% |
| Recall, category-blind | 67/97 = 69.1% | 77/97 = 79.4% | 77/97 = 79.4% |
| **Localization** (±15) | **73/97 = 75.3%** | 86/97 = 88.7% | 83/97 = 85.6% |
| Localization, blind | 89/97 = 91.8% | 93/97 = 95.9% | 91/97 = 93.8% |
| File-level | 96/97 = 99.0% | 97/97 = 100% | 97/97 = 100% |
| **Precision proxy**, aware | **16.5%** (47/285) | 12.5% (69/553) | 7.8% (70/892) |
| Findings | 285 | 553 | 892 |
| Distinct lines cited | 1,181 | 3,597 | 4,577 |
| Mean / max trace steps | 4.56 / 13 | 8.74 / 51 | 6.64 / 38 |
| Tokens | 9,381,580 | 9,618,943 | 9,668,297 |
| Cost | $24.85 | $4.37 | $17.01 |
| Runtime | 32m12s at C=8 | 13m04s at C=32 | ~18.5 min at C=32 |

`ai-llm-agency` scored **1/4** — the first non-zero on that class by any model here; both peers scored 0/4. `misconfiguration` at 3/17 is the weakest per-class figure in the file.

Single-variable against run 6: Stage 0.5's manifest is **identical** to it — same 865 lane ids, same 541-lane hunt set, same target files, zero lanes with differing assigned classes — so Stage 2's model is the only difference.

## Execution

541/541 hunt lanes, 865 consumption entries (541 hunt + 324 skip), 865 unique `lane_id`, **0 duplicates, 0 `failed: true`**, `exit_code 0`, `degraded: false`, `blocked_reads: 0`, 1,082 calls = exactly 2 per lane. Guards **226 passed, 0 failed**.

The run took three launches: container reclamation at 143 lanes; a 429 storm at `HUNT_CONCURRENCY=16` that lost 53 lanes; then a clean C=8 resume that finished 125/125 with 0 retries. The 53 lanes were correctly re-queued and all completed, so the scored artifact covers every lane. Program spend was 11,597,180 tokens across the three launches.

## Two corrections to the plan, both from measurement

**§9.4 — Gemini rate limiting.** The section previously said Gemini enforces spend-based limits (~$10/10 min) that stall "without a 429". Wrong on both counts, and it misdirected my own diagnosis. The binding limit is ordinary **TPM**, surfacing as a plain `429 status code (no body)`. Console figures at tier 1: **1,000 RPM / 2,000,000 TPM / 10,000 RPD**, with 28-day peaks of 232 RPM / 1.63M TPM / 2.36K RPD. That 1.63M peak is **82% of ceiling**, reached at C=16, against the runbook's standing 40–50% target. Per-unit throughput here is ~102k TPM — six times `luna`'s ~16k at the same effort — which puts the derived concurrency at 8.8, hence **8, a ceiling rather than a starting point**. Raising it to 16 was my decision and is the proximate cause of the lost lanes; that is stated in the row and in the archive, not buried.

Also recorded: `gemini31pro` at **25 RPM / 250 RPD** cannot complete 1,082 calls in a day at any concurrency.

**§9.7 — Gemini thinking tokens are billed but not counted.** `total_tokens` exceeds `prompt_tokens + completion_tokens`; the gap is thinking, which `models.json` says the vendor bills as output. On the final pass: 1,587,996 + 36,141 = 1,624,137 against `total_tokens` 1,963,904 — **339,767 unaccounted**. `costUsd()` prices `completion_tokens` alone, so `usage-v2.json` under-reports Gemini spend. The output column in the results file is visible output **plus** thinking, which is what makes it comparable to the `luna` and `glm52` columns.

## Stage 0 ran at default reasoning effort, Stage 2 at high

`stage0-recon/src/llm-probe.ts` hardcodes output caps of 500 and 5,000 rather than reading `outputTokenCap()`, while still spreading `samplingParams()`. Measured against the live endpoint with the verbatim prompts and real corpus files:

| probe | cap | effort | finish_reason | thinking | outcome |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| tool-calling (`routes/chat.ts`) | 500 | default | `stop` | — | parses |
| tool-calling (`routes/chat.ts`) | 500 | **high** | **`length`** | ~357 | truncated, `JSON.parse` fails |
| category (real arch summary) | 5000 | default | `stop` | 2,212 | parses |
| category (real arch summary) | 5000 | **high** | **`length`** | 2,427 | truncated |

On failure `markDegraded()` fires and Stage 0 falls back to deterministic analysis — a *different recon* that would later read as a model result. `llm-probe.ts:68` prints `[LLM OK]` **before** `JSON.parse`, so a truncated body still logs OK; `meta.json → degraded` is the only trustworthy signal. Default effort also matches run 6, whose Stage 0/0.5 came from run 3 and predate `reasoning_effort` existing. Stage 0 here recorded `degraded: false`.

- `docs/benchmarking-results.md` — **append only.** Every `luna` and `glm52` cell is byte-identical to `main`, §2.1 and §2.2 unchanged, rules and method sections unchanged; verified cell by cell rather than by eye. The sole removal is `gemini36flash`'s own row from §4 Pending, now recorded in §1.
